rationale: Mirrors the existing unconditional-detect-near-top shape already used by _run_yes() (cli.py:519) and run_tui() (tui.py:185); _apply_config() param addition matches its existing optional-keyword convention. Scored 11/12 vs Option B's 5/12 — Option B's config-plumbing approach has zero precedent for reading a value back across the plan/apply JSON-serialization boundary and runs against two established conventions (detection-only facts kept outside proposed_config; stale plan data recomputed fresh rather than trusted).
rule: Option A — call detect_installation() unconditionally near the top of _run_apply(), thread install_source into _apply_config() as a new parameter
alternatives_rejected: Option B: populate config["install_source"] in _run_plan() so _run_apply() reads it back without a second detect_installation() call
